text:
sara (product): Heads-up: drafting the PRD for the new quota + pricing semantics. need alignment on acceptance criteria and edge cases before i send to execs. any hot takes?

mike (eng): quick Q — are we doing hard-enforce or advisory-first rollout?

sara (product): prefer advisory for 2 weeks then opt-in hard enforcement. rollout plan in PRD. advisory = 429 + descriptive headers, no billing.

raj (billing): advisory period makes sense. we need metering semantics nailed so invoices don't surprise customers. suggest: meter tokens in 1s windows, round up to nearest token unit, expose daily usage CSV.

sasha (support): please add acceptance criteria for support tooling: customer-visible usage page + export + flagged overages. we get p0 tickets if people see unexpected charges.

mike (eng): implementation notes: will add rate limit headers: `X-Quota-Limit`, `X-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Quota-Reset`. also publish `GET /v1/limits` and `GET /v1/usage?range=30d`. example:```http
GET /v1/limits
200 OK
{
  "per_account": 1000000,
  "per_user": 50000,
  "window_seconds": 86400
}
```

eva (design): on the UI side: show both "estimated monthly spend" and "actual usage" prominently. add a tooltip about advisory vs enforced state. mockups incoming.

raj (billing): edge cases to define:
- shared API keys across orgs (how to attribute?)
- refunds for the advisory period if meter had a bug
- prorating when customers change plan mid-cycle
- promotion credits and how they apply to quotas

sara (product): good list. i'll add that as explicit edge-case acceptance criteria. also need decision on per-key vs per-identity enforcement — current thinking: enforcement by API key (primary) + optional per-user override for enterprise.

mike (eng): perf edge case: KV cache + batching can make token counts non-intuitive (we may prefetch/aggregate). acceptance criterion: quota meter must approximate actual billed tokens within 1% for high volume workloads or provide a deterministic mapping doc.

quota-bot: deploy notice: limits-service v2 will be rolled to staging at 2026-04-12T03:00Z.

sasha (support): also add clear runbook: show customers how to request temporary burst increases and how to opt-out of auto-enforce. we should script canned responses.

raj (billing): billing semantics: overage policy options = [charge-per-token, soft-allow then invoice, block]. need to pick default for self-serve vs enterprise. propose: self-serve = charge-per-token with rate caps; enterprise = contract-defined.

sara (product): decision for PRD: default = charge-per-token for self-serve with soft alert threshold (90%) + opt-in hard block. enterprise handled via contract. i'll capture in PRD.

mike (eng): acceptance checklist draft (short):
- APIs: `GET /v1/limits`, `GET /v1/usage`, `POST /v1/quotas` for config
- Headers on every response (`X-Quota-*`)
- Advisory mode emits internal telemetry + no billing changes
- Enforcement mode returns 429 and increments denial counter
- Billing CSV export matches metering within 1%
- UI mockups for usage and estimated spend
- Runbooks for support + opt-out flows

eva (design): adding mockup link: https://redwood.ex/mockups/quota-ui (private)

sara (product): perfect. action items:
- mike: tech spec + sample API contract by EOD Thu (1769980000)
- raj: billing mapping doc + refund policy draft by Mon (1770060000)
- eva: final mocks and tooltip copy by Fri
- sasha: draft canned support replies + runbook by Mon

mike (eng): noted. i also want to flag one more edge case: mixed workloads where embeddings + chat share same token budget. PRD must define per-product buckets vs global.

sara (product): yep — add as acceptance case: "support product-scoped quotas and a global fallback".

raj (billing): question: metering granularity for billing — do we bill per-token or per-1000 tokens? costing pipelines prefer per-1k to reduce invoice noise. propose meter in tokens, bill in units of 1000 with clear rounding rule.

mike (eng): agree. meter tokens raw, expose exact counts. billing does aggregation by 1000 with `round_up` semantics. put that in acceptance criteria.

sasha (support): quick QA ask: please include support test accounts that simulate high-volume bursts so we can validate tickets.

sara (product): adding to PRD test plan. final Q: any objections to advisory-first rollout + 2-week observation window?

raj (billing): no objections. logging a note to review invoices after window.

mike (eng): no objections.

eva (design): no objections :thumbsup:

sasha (support): :+1:

sara (product): thanks — i'll circulate the PRD draft with the acceptance checklist + edge-case table in ~2 hours. tagging owners in the doc.

mike (eng): thanks. will sketch API contract in thread once done.

quota-bot: ci:limits-tests passed (branch: quota/prd)

sara (product): awesome, closing for now. will reopen if anyone finds a blocker after reading the PRD."
